To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(d)TMs over FEF impaired search performance, and this effect was limited to the time period between 40 and80 msec after search onset.
(d)TMs over right FEF impaired target detection in a visual conjunction search task, and this impairment was limited to a narrow time window between 50 and 80 msec poststimulus.
(d)TMs over the right frontal eye field (FE) impairs visual target discrimination in human subjects during conjunction visual search.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional neuroanatomy of visual attention.
the role of frontal eye field (FEFF) in target discrimination.
the neural mechanisms underlying human visual attention.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FEF is a critical node in the neural network for visual target discrimination.
the FEF is a key structure in the human visual system, and that it is involved in visual processing, and not merely in the preparation of saccadic eye movements.
TMS over FEF impairs the ability of humans to discriminate targets from distractors in visual search, and that this effect is limited to a very specific time window.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the frontal eye field (FEFF) is involved in the early stages of target discrimination, which are independent of saccadic programming.
the frontal eye fields are not only important for saccadic eye movements but also for visual discrimination and target selection in humans.
the FEF plays an important role in visual processing, but not in the generation of saccades.

FEF neurons in humans are involved in visual target discrimination, and this is independent of sccade planning.
